Course and distance winner Amaysmont can be forgiven a flop latest when upped to a mile on turf and now back over what looks his optimum conditions can go very close

selections.comment: Caballo De Mar is in flying form and will be a tough nut to crack again seeking a five-timer. He should be able to translate his recent improvement back on Polytrack but a further 6lb rise might be enough to halt the winning streak in such a competitive heat and at likely cramped odds can be taken on. LIAM SWAGGER fits the bill. James Owen's gelding has himnself been in rude health of late (over both codes), including a terrific third at the Cheltenhham Festival when last seen in the 'Fred Winter' juvenile. He went close at Kempton in August off a two pound lower mark and has improved considerably since. Don Simon is worthy of note and on the pick of novice form should be bang there but it's a concern he was trounced on his sole handicap run. Perhpas the soft ground that day was too much of an inconvenience and if so he could be up to a task like this given the scope for improvement on only his sixth start but Knockbrex is preferred. Charlie Johnston's gelding shapes as if this trip will bring out his best and a peak effort looks on the cards

selections.comment: The hugely exciting SKY MAJESTY can stretch her unbeaten status to four races by landing this before going on to better and brighter things. The biggest question mark surrounds the suitability of Polytrack but she has seemed pretty versatile so far winning on heavy, good and good to firm in her three runs to date. A Group 3 and Group 2 winner already she sets the standard. Entitled to be a bit rusty she should still have enough here. The mian danger is Jouncy who was narrowly touched off in a G2 at Kempton last September before a creditable 5th of 6 in the G1 Grand Criterium when last seen. Perfect Part has decent place claims but most likely to shock the above couple is Sayidah Dariyan, a 13l winner over 6f on Polytrack (Lingfield) on second start. This is a differnet league but she can make her presence felt

selections.comment: A very trappy affair with most in with a shout. One that takes the eye is A MAJOR PAYNE who kicked of this campaign with a fine third over CD last time despite a moderate draw and coming from a bit far back. Micheal Bell's charge has enjoyed making it a couple of times and with scope for more and the plum draw he's the selection. Top-weight Gunlock finished 6th, a few lengths behind the selction, that day and while he had a race-fitness edge, he too was poorly drawn and couldn't get an early pitch in the vanguard as he prefers. He's a pound better off here and significantly gets a much better draw in 3 compared to 11 then. He can chase the selection. Lord Rapscallion merits consideration. Back to top form with a double over 7f and still 3lb shy of his last winning mark before this latest purple patch he can continue the fine form upped to a mile, a trip he hasn't tried for a long while but has had winning form over earlier in his career

selections.comment: NOTIMEFORCHITCHAT has the strongerst looking cliams in a fiendishly tough closer. The Time Test gelding scraped home last time over 7f but finished powerfully and the step up to 1m2f today if anything copuld bring out more (he won over 1m as a juvenile). A big run can be expected. Dalmally will have his supporters having opened his account when last seen in October and kicks off his handicap career off a fair looking mark. A close second here augurs well but a tough double-figure draw adds to the task and Say What You See appeals more. He impressed when powering to an eight length win on penultimate start and should relish the step up to 1m2f. If he copes with the artificial Polytrack as well as he did Tapeta he's entitled to go close. One who might go under the radar with a sporting chance is Golden Garden. Form figures of 964 don't inspire confidence but Jamie Osborne's gelding has improved with each run and now up in trip off a potentially lenient opening mark can reward each way backers.

selections.comment: Multiple C&D winner SUN DANCER GIRL can continue her consistent level of form and fine record here for a yard flying at the moment. She ran into an in form rival who has followed up last time and gets to race off only 1lb higher here with the assistance of a claimer who was successful on his last ride. Destinado has been inconsistent throughout his career but cashed in on a reduced mark last time benefitting from a pace collapse. He's never won a mark as high as this revised one but with the longer trip in his his favour isn't ruled out. Raintown has a fine record here and arrives in good form. If able to get across from his wide draw with little other competition up front, he could be tough to catch.

Tuco Salamanca failed to stay a strongly run mile last time but had proven progressive previously at 7f. This may be on the sharp side but the combination of the track and likely strong pace can see him stay on into a place. Coul Angel beat The Flying Seagull last time but may struggle to confirm that on these revised terms, with the latter best forgiven his subsequent run where nothing went right.

selections.comment: Andrew Balding has started the season in flying form and holds a strong hand here with Humam, Marchogion and Berkshire Whisper. The latter looks the first string on jockey bookings but has plenty to find with Megaphone on their previous meeting. The former is already a tapeta winner and has held a consistent level of form since going handicapping so should give a good account once more. David Probert's charge was behind Carbine Harvester and So Darn Hot last time but he was given far too much to do that day looking an unlucky loser. If ridden slightly more positively he could reverse that form. HELLO ZAMAN showed a willing attitude in defeat last time and the well backed favourite that day has boosted the form at Group level. He can take advantage of a lenient opening mark in an open race.

selections.comment: The top of the weights is probably the way to go here and CLOUD COVER may be able to repeat the success of 2024 off a 14lb higher mark. She has been hugely progressive for some time and produced a career best when taking the Prix Miss Satixma in the autumn. She matched that with an easy win when returned to handicaps at the start of the year and has only been raised 3lb for that. Though it is odd she has had a wind op since she can continue her fine course record. Aramis Grey had the benefit of a draw bias when midfield on turf last time but she has shown a consistent level of form for some time and holds each way claims back up in trip. Powdering has won 2 of her last 4 on the AW and a 1lb rise for her narrow latest defeat looks lenient. She can complete the places.

selections.comment: James Fanshawe boasts a strong hand here with Heathcliff and WILLIAM TWEE. The former was a C&D winner last summer and is worth forgiving his latest run where he was badly snatched up at a key stage. He rates a danger back over his optimum trip but it is his stablemate who appeals most. He is a former Listed winner who was poorly positioned off a steady pace over a stretching trip last time but will find this stiff 6f more to his liking. With cheekpieces applied for the first time he holds strong claims from below his last winning mark. Recent Kachy winner Marshman has his held form well at higher levels of late and is very much respected off top weight holding a big class edge. Of those at bigger prices Coachello could go well off just 1lb higher than his last winning mark. He was given far too much to do and raced against the track bias last time but was far from disgraced.

selections.comment: ROARING LEGEND has been thriving since being upped to staying trips after returning from a spell jumping and is expected to continue his progress and defy top weight. Though he got first run last time he drew clear easily and that race has produced a trio of next time out winners so this 8lb higher mark shouldn't be beyond him. Wonder Legend got the run of the race from the front last time when defeating Plage De Harve but may struggle to confirm that form with the unexposed stayer with a stronger pace likely here. Though Duke Of Oxford has developed into something of a Kempton specialist he did place over this C&D in the Northumberland Plate last year so is feared in his hat trick bid.
